questions.problem: Using the definition of the hyperbolic cosine, calculate ${f}^{-1}(x)$ given that $f(x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡(x+1)$ and $x\ge -1.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $y=\operatorname{cosh}⁡(x+1).$ Since $x\ge -1,$ we have $y\ge 1.$

To find the inverse function we swap $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
x=\operatorname{cosh}⁡(y+1),
$$

where $x\ge 1$ and $y\ge -1.$

Next, we apply the definition of $\operatorname{cosh}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{y+1}+{e}^{-(y+1)}) \\ 2x & ={e}^{y+1}+{e}^{-(y+1)} \\ 2x{e}^{y+1} & ={e}^{2(y+1)}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Bringing everything to the left-hand side, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2(y+1)}-2x{e}^{y+1}+1 & =0 \\ {({e}^{y+1})}^{2}-2x({e}^{y+1})+1 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $Y={e}^{y+1}.$ We can form a quadratic equation in $Y$ and solve it by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Y}^{2}-2xY+1 & =0 \\ (Y-x)^{2}-{x}^{2}+1 & =0 \\ (Y-x)^{2} & ={x}^{2}-1 \\ Y-x & =\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}-1} \\ Y & =x\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}-1} \\ {e}^{y+1} & =x\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}-1} \\ y+1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}-1})\end{aligned}
$$

Note that for  $x\ge 1,$ we have $x-\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}\le 1$ and  $x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}\ge 1.$ Since $y+1\ge 0,$ the logarithm in the above equality must be non-negative. This requires its argument to be greater than or equal to $1$ for $x\ge 1$, so we reject the alternative with the negative sign. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}y+1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1})-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1})-1.
$$
